title: Grateful Dead Live at The Warehouse on 1970-01-31
lineage: SBD > MR > C > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording (some hiss) captures a rare acoustic‑rich show with standout gems like Saw Mill, Hard to Handle and Katie May.
ai_review.review: The SBD source delivers an acceptably clear picture of a memorable early‑1970 concert – the acoustic set is repeatedly praised for its rarity and emotion, highlighted by songs such as Saw Mill, Hard to Handle and the soaring Katie May performance.  While a little hiss and occasional amp trouble are noted, the band’s energy (especially Jerry’s guitar intensity) shines through, making this a highly valued entry for collectors.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews are 4‑5 stars and overwhelmingly positive about the performance and rare acoustic material; recording quality is described as good with only minor hiss, supporting a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Standard SBD clarity with some hiss noted; generally acceptable and listenable despite occasional noise.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The concert is split between a solid electric portion and an especially praised acoustic set; Phil's bass amp mishap forced a shift that resulted in a rare, emotionally rich acoustic second set.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Noted for strong guitar intensity on Hard to Handle and overall amazing playing.
band_member_comments.Phil: His amp blew during the show, yet he kept professional; bass issues are mentioned but his performance is still respected.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen is highlighted as returning to organ duties, adding depth to the acoustic set.
